title: Human Development and Family Studies, B.S. — Life Span Human Services Option (College of Health and Human Development)
notes:
2026-09-17 historical-year build for the 2022-2023 catalog edition. Fetched the real archived page (bulletins.psu.edu/archive/2022-2023/undergraduate/colleges/health-human-development/human-development-family-studies-bs/, raw curl + BeautifulSoup text extraction) and diffed it line-by-line against the 2023-2024 archive built in HDFS-2023.json. Finding: 2022-2023's Program Requirements, option names ('Life Span Human Services Option'/'Life Span Developmental Science Option'), course-by-course lists, and Suggested Academic Plan are IDENTICAL to 2023-2024's -- same prescribed HDFS 129/301/311/312W/315/418, same Statistics pool, same 43-45 credit Life Span Human Services option structure (prescribed HDFS 411/414/455, the 428/429/433/445 pool, the 300-/400-level HDFS block, the 13-15 credit internship/practicum pathway, and the 12-credit unenumerated Supporting Courses block), same '73-76' major-credit and '119-121' plan-total figures. Copied HDFS-2023.json's semesters array verbatim (only catalog_year/source/notes differ), same as how CMPSC's own unchanged consecutive years are handled. The only real differences found between the two editions are non-curricular: (1) generic University-wide General Education boilerplate wording differs (2022's Gen Ed section describes 'Knowledge Domains' at 6 credits each domain under an older Gen Ed framework description vs. 2023's 3-credits-each 'Breadth in the Knowledge Domains' language reflecting a university-wide Gen Ed framework rewrite) -- this is University Bulletin-wide boilerplate repeated on every program's page, not an HDFS-specific requirement change, and it does not touch the Suggested Academic Plan table itself (verified identical, zero diff lines in that section between the two editions' extracted text); (2) academic-advising contact names/emails/department URLs differ (personnel changes only, not modeled in this app's plan JSON). Campus check for this catalog year: the archived page's own 'Where can I complete this program?' section lists the identical campus set as 2023-2024 -- 'Degree Information At Additional Campuses: Altoona, Brandywine, DuBois, Fayette, Harrisburg, Mont Alto, Scranton, Shenango, York', and 'Life Span Human Services Option -- Available at the following campuses: Altoona, Brandywine, DuBois, Fayette, Harrisburg, Mont Alto, Scranton, Shenango, University Park, World Campus, York' -- Brandywine confirmed Pattern A (same curriculum) for 2022-2023 as well. Erie/Behrend is absent from every campus list on this page too -- HDFS was not offered at Erie in 2022-2023 either, consistent with all 5 catalog years checked this session.

Self-verification finding (real, not a data error, same as HDFS-2023.json since this file copies its structure): the remaining requirements after the common-core semesters are almost entirely 400-level HDFS courses (HDFS 411/414/418/428-445 pool/455/490), which hit this app's real Faculty Senate Policy 34-00 registration-standing gate (planner_engine.py's standing_gate_ok/semester_standing) when placed too early -- a 400-level course is only recommended once the simulated student's real, catalog-matched completed credits cross the 5th-semester threshold. Fixed the same way as HDFS-2023.json: the 300-/400-level HDFS elective block and Supporting Courses block are modeled as 'open_elective' slots (real catalog courses, prefer_prefixes: HDFS) instead of bare course-less placeholders, and the six 400-level required items are grouped into Semesters 7-8 instead of 5-6, after five terms of real coursework have banked well past the 60-credit 5th-semester threshold. Verified via a full USE_OLLAMA=0 build_full_plan simulation: 0 'Could not schedule' warnings.
